diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Thamaneh Ghadarkhan, a journalist, reported an increase in the share of direct out-of-pocket healthcare expenses by patients. She said access to treatment has decreased for a large part of the population, and the high cost of medicine and healthcare services has led even the middle class to forgo some or all of their treatment. The healthcare system in Iran is moving towards a class-based treatment system.

A group of officials from the Raisi and Ahmadinejad governments and current parliament members called for halting cooperation and starting the legal process for Iran's exit from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. They consider continued participation in the treaty not in the country's interest. Signatories include Heydar Moslehi and Masoud Zaribafan.

A video shows that Azadi Stadium is still without grass, with drainage and groundwork ongoing. Some stands behind the goal remain without seats. The stadium was supposed to be ready for the 1405-1406 season, but the complete replacement of the grass has delayed the preparation process.

The United Students channel reported the ban on entry of 150 students at Alzahra University. For many of these students, no disciplinary committee ruling was issued, and the ban was enforced without written notification by the university president's order. Some of these students have been banned since last semester, exceeding the two-month period set in the disciplinary regulations.

Michael Parsa, Ontario's Minister of Children, said that officials of the Islamic Republic should be ashamed of support coming from far outside Iran. He made these remarks at the unveiling ceremony of a plaque and bench commemorating the Lion and Sun Revolution. He emphasized that people outside Iran care more about the Iranian people than the government does.

The US dollar exchange rate in Iran's open market surpassed 240,000 tomans on October 6, 2026. The euro reached 273,000 tomans and the British pound reached 318,000 tomans. Additionally, the price of the new Emami coin rose to 242 million tomans.

China and the United States agreed to mutually reduce tariffs on goods worth about 30 billion dollars after a meeting between their presidents. This agreement was reached following the meeting of Xi Jinping and Donald Trump. The report includes an interview with Alireza Mohibi, a journalist from Iran International.

Videos received by Iran International show the presence of armed forces in a girls' technical school in Andisheh city. This presence was for a symbolic funeral of Ali Khamenei on Sunday, the fifth of Mehr. The event was reported on a specific date.

A group of Iranians living in Canada gathered in front of Calgary City Hall, demanding the halt of executions for Ali Zarei, Aref Khamseh, and other political prisoners. They also commemorated two teenagers killed during the "Woman, Life, Freedom" uprising. This report was prepared by Sepidar Valian from Iran International.

The brother of Esmail Beigi, a protester killed in January, responded to Masoud Pezeshkian's remarks at the UN, accusing him of baselessly calling his brother an armed terrorist. He emphasized that his brother was unarmed and nonviolent when killed. Esmail Beigi was shot and killed by snipers in Isfahan on January 9.

Mehdi Taj announced that the new head coach of Iran's U23 football team will be introduced within two days. The aim is for the U23 coach to closely supervise the youth teams. Iran's U23 team was eliminated from advancing in the 2026 Asian Games after losing to North Korea.

Melissa Lantsman, deputy leader of Canada's Conservative Party, attended the unveiling ceremony of the memorial plaque and bench for the immortal heroes of the Lion and Sun Revolution. She stated that the Islamic Republic wants these heroes to be forgotten, but they will not allow it. Lantsman also called for the expulsion of Islamic Republic agents from Canada.

A video shows an explosion caused by neutralizing leftover war ammunition on Kharg Island on Monday, October 6. The district governor of Kharg stated that the operation to neutralize unexploded shells and ammunition will last about 10 days.

The US Embassy in London asked American citizens to exercise caution after the arrest of several individuals on charges of attempting to bomb near Royal Air Force Fairford. The embassy stated that US-related facilities, gatherings, and organizations may be at increased risk. It also reminded American citizens that British authorities assess the terrorism threat level as severe.

Ben Sabti, a researcher on Iran and Israel, said Netanyahu's trip to the UAE may have a security purpose. Israel and the UAE likely discussed defense systems and intelligence cooperation. The meeting aimed for greater coordination against the Islamic Republic.

Alireza Arafi, in a message on the second anniversary of Hassan Nasrallah's death, stated that the ultimate victory over enemies and the destruction of Israel and the US is the inevitable fate of the resistance front. He emphasized that the resistance front from Tehran to Beirut and Gaza to Sanaa is a unified front. This unity is based on shared faith, enemy, and goals.

Ramin Ahmadzadeh won the silver medal in the under 81 kg Kurash category. Noshad Alamian reached the semifinals in table tennis and earned a bronze medal. This report was provided by Alireza Modiri from Iran International.

Benjamin Netanyahu, the Prime Minister of Israel, made a secret trip by private plane to Abu Dhabi and met with Mohammed bin Zayed. The meeting lasted four hours. Netanyahu had previously traveled secretly to Abu Dhabi during Operation "Roar of the Lions."

A video shows military vehicles stationed on Sunday, October 5, at a technical school in Tehran. One of the military personnel threatened the students in a speech. He warned them not to stand in the path of the enemy.

Hooman Shayani, a political detainee, remains in judicial limbo after 9 months of detention in Noorabad Mamasani prison. No trial has been held to address his charges so far. His family is unable to pursue the case due to financial difficulties and his mother's condition.
A video shows that Basij forces were present in a school in the country on Sunday, the fifth of Mehr. The video was received by Iran International. No further details have been provided.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial board, referring to Donald Trump's remarks about ending the Iran war, said Trump seeks US interests with 'minimum cost and maximum benefit' and, through maximum pressure, aims to secure 'maximum concessions' at the negotiating table. He added that Trump will not end the current situation until he guarantees full security of the Strait of Hormuz and the return of shipping to pre-war conditions, whether through continued economic pressure or by resuming war to bring the Islamic Republic back to negotiations.

Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei, head of the judiciary, ordered strict action against laxity and nudity. He emphasized that this issue should be handled with prudence and planning, avoiding any actions against religious law and regulations. The presidents of the parliament and the republic also agree and should not fear the uproar.

A video has been released showing a citizen cleaning and placing flowers on the tombstones of Peyman Manzhesafat, Ilya Dehqani, Mohammad Rezaei, and Milad Bahadri. These four protesters were shot by officers on January 9, 2026. Ilya Dehqani died in the hospital one week after being injured.

The Argentine court in 2024 declared the AMIA bombing in Buenos Aires a crime against humanity. The court stated the operation was ordered by the Islamic Republic and carried out by Hezbollah Lebanon. The 1994 bombing resulted in 85 deaths and over 300 injuries.

Ali Alipour won the gold medal in the men's 95 kg weightlifting category at the Asian Games with a total of 398 kg. He lifted 180 kg in the snatch and 218 kg in the clean and jerk, breaking the Asian Games record and the world total record. This gold medal was the eighth gold for the Iranian team at the Nagoya Asian Games.
ISNA news agency reported that Bijan Mortazavi, a pop singer and musician, entered Iran at the beginning of the week. This news has been implicitly confirmed but not officially announced yet.

Reuters reported that the connection of the attack near the Royal Air Force base in Fairford to the Islamic Republic is considered the most likely option. The possibility of sabotage by Russia or Islamist groups is also being investigated. A threat from the Islamic Republic against this base was raised about six weeks ago.

Sergey Lavrov stated that Russia may agree to transfer Turkey's S-400 missile defense systems to another friendly country. This agreement is conditional on Russia's explicit consent. It is also guaranteed that these systems will not be transferred to a third country, especially Ukraine.

The French foreign minister stated that France's military mission to protect the Yanbu oil terminal in Saudi Arabia is purely defensive. He emphasized that France is not involved in the war with Iran. These remarks were made in an interview with an Iran International reporter.

Drugs related to coagulation disorders in women have not been imported into the country for about 11 months. Patients have been forced to use older and less effective methods. This drug shortage causes serious physical and psychological effects for women.

Turkey Today reported from two sources that all flights from Iran to Turkey are expected to be canceled early next month. Turkish officials have not announced this decision yet. A source close to Iran's aviation industry has also confirmed the possible cancellation.
Ali Mohammad Baghshahi, a clinical psychology student at Beheshti University, was released from Yazd prison on bail. This happened yesterday. More information is available from Harana News Agency.
A video shows IRGC agents training children, whose schools are closed, to use weapons. The video was received by Iran International. The video highlights military training given to children.

Mahbubeh Shabani, a detainee from the January 2026 protests sentenced to death, was transferred to solitary confinement in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. The transfer was carried out with violence. This event took place on Monday, October 6.

Investigations into the attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline have reached their final stages. According to reports, the perpetrators entered Iraq from Iran and launched drones from Maysan province. The Iraqi Foreign Ministry sent related information to Tehran but received no response.

Mojtaba Khamenei stated in a message that Iran is the fourth superpower in the world and, according to divine calculations, is the first power globally. He added that enemy forces do not advance beyond the Arabian Sea due to strikes by fighters and Hormuz Strait defenders. Additionally, over 30 million Iranians have declared their sacrifice, and a 500,000-person capacity was filled within the first 100 minutes of the call-up.

Amnesty International described the suppression of the "Women, Life, Freedom" uprising in the provinces of Kurdistan, Kermanshah, and West Azerbaijan as systematic and ruthless. The IRGC and police forces confronted protesters with military weapons. The organization called the killing of protesters a crime against humanity.

A group of teachers and healthcare workers have announced their resignation due to livelihood problems in videos. The number of such videos has recently increased. This issue has been reflected on social media.

Hamid Rasaei has been sentenced to 10 months of imprisonment for spreading falsehoods with intent to harm others. This sentence was issued and finalized by the Special Clergy Appeals Court. He has been transferred to the special clergy ward of Evin prison to serve his sentence.

A group of Allameh students held a protest gathering in Tehran on Tuesday, October 6. This news is based on videos received by Iran International. The location and exact time of the gathering were announced in Tehran.

Students report unpaid wages and insufficient training during internships. Glass factory workers in Qazvin have not received their wages due to financial corruption and debt. There are also reports of delayed payments in Mahshahr and sharp price increases in Tehran and Kermanshah.

During the 'Woman, Life, Freedom' uprising, security forces killed protesters not only in the streets but also in homes and detention centers. Ramin Fatehi was one of the protesters who died under torture after being arrested by the IRGC Intelligence. Iran International interviewed his sister seeking justice.

Jabbar Azarhomayoun was transferred to Sanandaj prison after more than three weeks of detention and completion of interrogation. He was held in the Intelligence Department detention center. This transfer to Sanandaj prison has taken place.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing the noise disturbance caused by a government night gathering in Boumehen. The video was submitted as a local report. The issue of noise disturbance in this area has been highlighted.

The US Embassy in London issued a security warning after several people were arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist operation near the RAF Fairford base. The embassy urged American citizens to review their personal security plans. The level of terrorist threats in the UK has been declared high.

Mediators are scheduled to hold separate talks with the US and the Islamic Republic on Monday or Tuesday. Abbas Araghchi and Qatari mediators are present in the US. The talks will focus on a revised version of a seven-day proposal previously presented by the Islamic Republic.

The UK Defense Minister stated that the Islamic Republic and its proxy forces intend to harm the UK. Five people were arrested near RAF Fairford airbase, with Iran-related motives considered the most likely hypothesis. Tehran has denied any involvement in these matters.

In the first five months of the year, 185 people died in traffic accidents in Mazandaran, with 132 deaths occurring on suburban and rural roads. The highest fatalities were recorded in Sari, Babol, and Amol. Additionally, the number of accident injuries increased by 21% compared to last year, while the number of deaths decreased by 4%.

The daughters of the immortal Hamid Shakarian joined the campaign "One Candle, One Memory, One Name" by lighting a candle. They stated that they will continue in memory of the immortal ones of the homeland. This act was done in memory of their father.

The US Central Command denied claims by an IRGC official about full control of the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM stated that the Iranian naval forces have been sunk and no naval force remains. The free passage of ships through the strait indicates that Iran does not control this waterway.

The price of the dollar in Iran's free market increased by more than 6,000 tomans on Monday, reaching 242,500 tomans. The euro approached 276,000 tomans and the British pound reached 318,600 tomans. Fars news agency attributed the currency rate increase to statements by the US Treasury Secretary and dealer activities.

Mike Waltz, the US representative to the United Nations, stated that Washington rejected Iran's seven-day ceasefire proposal and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz due to Iran's conditions. These conditions included access to billions of dollars in frozen assets and lifting sanctions. Waltz mentioned this in an interview with NBC News.

Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei, head of the judiciary, called on the Attorney General to confront the state of nudity decisively and with planning. He stated that the president and parliament also agree with confronting nudity. This request was made in a meeting on Monday, the 6th of Mehr.

The Iranian embassy in London denied any connection between Iran and the arrest of five suspects near the RAF Fairford base, calling the speculations baseless. The embassy stated that such claims fuel Iranophobia propaganda and reserved the right to legal responses. Earlier, Reuters had suggested a possible link between the attack and the Islamic Republic.

Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Foreign Minister, is scheduled to meet with the mediators of the negotiations with the US on Monday morning. No US representative will attend this meeting, which will focus on reviewing the latest proposals and views on the negotiation conditions. Iran has proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the release of its frozen assets.

Andy Burnham, the UK Prime Minister, announced that following the arrest of five British citizens suspected of plotting an attack on the RAF Fairford base, an emergency Cobra security meeting will be held. The arrests took place over the weekend. The Fairford airbase is used by the United States.
Bijan Mortazavi denied news of his return to Iran. He called the reports by some media outlets false. This response was published in a video on his Instagram story.

At least 23 female prisoners in Evin Prison have been deprived of family visits for three to nine weeks due to protests against conditions and treatment by guards. Golrokh Iraee and Sakineh Parvaneh have each been banned for nine weeks, and Ghazal Marzban for seven weeks. Other prisoners have been banned from visits for three weeks.

British counter-terrorism police announced that five men connected to the incident at the Fairford airbase were released on bail after interrogation. Investigations continue, and strict restrictions on their movements have been imposed. The police are also examining the possibility that they acted on behalf of a foreign government.

A student told Iran International in a video that studying in Iran has become possible only for the wealthy class. He mentioned the high prices of stationery and difficulties in education. Families cannot afford the costs of education.

The Israeli army announced that Shadi Abu Hasira, the main financier of Hamas's military wing, was killed in an airstrike in Gaza. Abu Hasira managed the "Geneva" exchange network and the "Gardena Professional" company, which financed Hamas. Israel called these actions a violation of the ceasefire and will continue targeting financial infrastructure.

Retired telecommunications workers held protest gatherings in Ahvaz and Isfahan. They demand supplementary insurance without deductibles and implementation of salary adjustments according to the law. They also seek payment of overdue claims and attention to medical and livelihood issues.

Ed Miliband, the UK Foreign Secretary, described recent threats at the Royal Air Force base as reminders of ongoing dangers. He emphasized that London will counter these with economic sanctions and actions against Iran's proxy forces. Miliband called reopening the Strait of Hormuz essential to address the cost of living crisis in the UK.

On Tuesday, October 6, the price of the US dollar increased by more than five thousand tomans to 245,000 tomans. The euro was 278,500 tomans and the British pound was 325,000 tomans. Also, the Turkish lira surpassed five thousand tomans for the first time, and the price of the new Imam coin exceeded 247 million tomans.

The One Million Signatures campaign started in 2006 and brought the issue of legal discrimination and women's rights into the public sphere. It transformed women's rights demands from a limited request to a social demand. Activists' pressure in 2008 led to the revision of the Family Protection Bill and the removal of two controversial articles.

Iran International has obtained exclusive documents showing that Mostafa Ahadi, a senior figure in the IRGC intelligence organization, organizes a corruption network in Iran's oil sales. He and Sardar Moshfegh have ordered the removal of news related to trust corruption. This information was reported by Mojtaba Pourmohsen.

A US official told CNN on Monday that Donald Trump is ready to reduce sanctions on Iran and release frozen assets in exchange for 'tangible progress' toward a nuclear deal. The official said the US is engaged in 'positive and constructive talks' through intermediaries but stressed that no deal will be reached until nuclear issues are resolved.

Donald Trump is ready to reduce sanctions and release blocked assets in exchange for specific steps by Iran regarding its nuclear program. Qatari and Pakistani mediators are trying to reach an agreement between Iran and the US. Disagreements remain over nuclear issues and the timing of commitments.

The Trump administration is considering issuing a limited sanctions exemption to resume flights for Shia pilgrims between Iran and Najaf. This exemption would allow Iraqi Airways to operate flights for one month. A longer-term exemption may be issued after this period.

Ali Hasan Bahamin, Ali Safari, and Hojat Sadat, three detained teacher activists in Noorabad Mamasani, were released on bail. They were arrested on Friday, 3 Mehr. They were detained along with three other individuals by security forces.

The Iran Prosperity Project, initiated by the National Union for Democracy in Iran, will be presented at a meeting in the European Parliament in Brussels. The meeting will review proposals and plans for political transition in Iran. Topics include governance, security, territorial integrity, and continuity of essential services.

Reza Dormishian, a writer and film director, has been summoned to Branch 7 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. The summons was issued on September 22. He is required to appear in court on October 20, 2026.

Four workers in the Faramane Industrial Town of Kermanshah were injured due to unsafe working conditions. The incident was caused by inadequate workplace safety. More details have been published by Harana News Agency.

Reports indicate an increase in the sale of second-hand personal and household items in Iran. The market for new goods is sluggish while second-hand sales are booming. This occurs alongside warnings about the expanding economic problems faced by people.
A citizen reported being unemployed for several weeks in a video to Iran International. He expressed despair and uncertainty about what to do next. The video reflects economic concerns.

An informed source stated that prisoners in various wards of Tehran's Great Prison face violent behavior from the prison's inspection chief. This includes political prisoners. The prisoners' protests have so far gone unanswered.

Abbas Araghchi and the Iranian delegation are scheduled to meet with mediators for negotiations with the US in New York. The mediators will separately negotiate with representatives from Tehran and Washington on Monday or Tuesday. The talks will focus on a revised version of the seven-day proposal presented by the Islamic Republic.
SpaceX's Starship rocket entered Earth's orbit for the first time. One of its engines failed, but the flight continued. This test flight is an important step for future missions to the Moon and Mars.

Al Hadath network reported, citing its sources, that the Islamic Republic has agreed to halt uranium enrichment in exchange for a reduction in US sanctions. According to these sources, mediators are pressuring the Islamic Republic to make concessions regarding its nuclear program.

Amir Ghalenoei stated in the pre-match press conference against Russia that the national team had insufficient time for tactical training. He emphasized the importance of the Russia game for preparing the team for the Asian Cup and mentioned a change in the playing style. He also expressed happiness about Sardar Azmoun's return to the national team.

The Football Federation's board did not decide on awarding the previous season's league trophy to Esteghlal in the Tuesday meeting. Esteghlal's request and the federation's promise to award the trophy have become a fruitless controversy. The next meeting will decide on the champion of the last season and awarding the trophy.

Scott Bassett, the US Treasury Secretary, stated that the economic exclusion operation has caused the rial to reach its lowest historical value. He added that the US will continue to weaken the Islamic Republic's ability to finance terrorism and develop nuclear weapons.

Farzin Nadimi stated that the increase in tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz indicates a decline in the Islamic Republic's ability to control shipping. The IRGC forces have faced intelligence and operational failures. The Islamic Republic is trying to reduce tensions through intermediaries and indirect talks.

The price of the dollar in Iran's open market has reached about 245,000 tomans. Official institutions have reported food inflation exceeding 120 percent, leading to a phenomenon called shoplifting in stores. This includes theft of cheese, butter, and cream.

A citizen stated in a video that the price of goods purchased in Iraqi Kurdistan is half the price of the same goods in Iran. Sellers emphasized that the fruits came from Iran. This report was published by Iran International.

Abbas Araghchi will meet with mediators of Tehran-Washington negotiations in New York today. The talks focus on Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the release of blocked assets. Araghchi stated that without fulfilling the conditions, Iran will not agree to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Mikaeil Dudkanlu Milan, a citizen of Mahabad, was released today from Naqadeh prison on bail.

Donald Trump stated that the US will soon win the war with Iran and gasoline prices will sharply decrease afterward. He also said the US has prevented Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons. Trump added that US officials have held talks with Iranian intermediaries.

Contract employees in the service sections of Golestan province's medical universities hospitals reported not receiving their bonuses for the past year. They expressed concern about the reduction in their wages. These employees have demanded attention to their situation.

Habibollah Sayari stated that the Strait of Hormuz is effectively closed, despite enemy claims that it is open. He emphasized that southern forces must be ready to prevent any enemy entry into the territory. Sayari also mentioned that the issue of revenge against enemies remains and must be carried out at any time and place.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad criticized Mojtaba Khamenei's statements on the program "Cheshmandaz," saying the claim that the Islamic Republic is the "world's top power" contradicts Mojtaba's hidden status. He added that Mojtaba's whereabouts are unknown, highlighting the gap between the government's claims and reality.

The audio version of Cheshmandaz announced that Mojtaba Khamenei referred to himself as a superpower from his hideout. This news was published by Iran International. No further details are provided in the text.

Mai Sato, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in Iran, emphasized the need for a legal moratorium on executions until the complete abolition of the death penalty after two years of her mission. She announced that from tomorrow until October 10, she will provide daily updates on cases related to executions. These cases mainly involve detainees from protests and those sentenced to death for various crimes.

Arghavan Rezaei, a former tennis player of Iranian descent living in France, has become the coach of Iran's tennis team for the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya. This was announced in an interview with Saeedeh Fathi, a sports journalist.

Press TV, quoting an informed Iranian official, reported that claims about Tehran's flexibility on the nuclear stance are incorrect. The official stated that the US is trapped in the Strait of Hormuz and is raising the nuclear issue to divert attention. It was also emphasized that Iran's position on the nuclear issue has not changed and no talks are currently underway.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said on Monday, September 28, 2026, at the White House that the US would win the war with the Islamic Republic 'very soon' and gas prices would drop sharply after the war. He added, 'No one else could have done this.' He also stated that the US has prevented Tehran from obtaining nuclear weapons.
The audio version of program 24 with Fardad Farahzad has been released. It covers the meeting of Araqchi with mediators in New York. This meeting is discussed in the news program.

Murad Vaisi said Mojtaba Khamenei's message claiming the Islamic Republic is the world's superpower shows his disconnect from Iran's economic and social realities. He cited power and gas crises, currency devaluation, oil sales restrictions, and flight cancellations as evidence against these claims. He also stated that Islamic Republic officials feel concern towards Reza Pahlavi.

Sardar Azmoun commented on the national team's performance in the 2026 World Cup, expressing disappointment over not advancing to the next stage. He admitted the team did not achieve good results and hopes to make up for it in the future. He also mentioned that criticism from Amir Ghalenoei about his physical readiness has become normal for him.

Ali Sadrzadeh said Benjamin Netanyahu's trip to Abu Dhabi shows the closeness between Israel and the UAE. The trip occurred while Netanyahu is under pressure from reports about warnings before the October 7 attack. Netanyahu aims to reduce political pressure ahead of the elections.

The US Senate subcommittee reported that the cryptocurrency Tether has become a tool for financing the Islamic Republic and its proxy groups. The report shows that 84% of wallets linked to Iran conducted transactions primarily with Tether. Tether responded by stating its commitment to cooperate with the US government and has blocked millions of dollars linked to Iran.

The 2026 Vaclav Havel Human Rights Prize was awarded to Nasrin Sotoudeh, an Iranian human rights lawyer, for her defense of human rights and opposition to compulsory hijab and the death penalty. The prize was presented at the autumn plenary session of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe in Strasbourg. Mehraveh Khandan Harris, Sotoudeh's daughter, received the award on her behalf.

Mostafa Ahadi, a senior official of the IRGC Intelligence Organization, manages a corruption network in the sale of Iran's sanctioned oil. The case of indebted trusts has been returned to the IRGC Intelligence Organization by order of the Supreme National Security Council. A confidential meeting was held to prevent the publication of news about the trusts' corruption.

Alireza Beiranvand explained his military service medical exemption request, with his medical commission session scheduled for October 5. The military has allowed him to continue sports activities until October 12. He denied any mental health exemption and stated that postponing military service is his legal right.

Donald Trump denied reports about offering to reduce sanctions on Iran in exchange for nuclear steps by Tehran. He stated that he did not make any offer to lift sanctions on Iran. These remarks came after a report by Axios.

Morad Vaisi said Mojtaba Khamenei is more delusional than Ali Khamenei. He believes those who consider Iran the fourth superpower are mistaken. According to him, Iran is the first superpower in the world.

The Syrian state oil company announced that on Monday evening, an explosion occurred at a gas pipeline valve between Al-Shoula and Deir Ezzor. The explosion was due to sabotage and stopped gas transfer to power plants. Firefighters isolated the area and continue extinguishing the fire.

A diplomatic source from the Islamic Republic said the US president does not have a clear stance on his demands from the negotiations. This has made it difficult to reach a specific agreement. Trump also stated that the US will soon win the war with the Islamic Republic.

Esmail Baghai announced that the Islamic Republic's delegation will leave New York for Tehran on Tuesday night as planned. A meeting was held with the Qatari delegation on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly to discuss regional developments. No detailed talks took place, and media reports were described as mere speculation.

Mai Sato, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in Iran, called for a halt to executions until the complete abolition of the death penalty. She announced that from Tuesday until October 9, she will provide updates on execution cases. Sato also highlighted the significant gap between Iran's judicial processes and international fair trial standards.

Leila Morvati said reports about a major change in Iran's nuclear policy should be viewed with skepticism until an official announcement. She added that withdrawing from uranium enrichment would be a turning point. Morvati emphasized that stopping enrichment alone will not resolve the crisis with the US.

Ghassan Ashour said the suspension and then limited resumption of flights between Iran and Iraq indicate a bargaining process by the Iraqi prime minister with Tehran and Washington. Baghdad gained a major concession by stopping Iranian flights and gave a limited concession by allowing Iraqi flights to Iran. Iraq's request to the US for a limited exemption for Iranian flights to Najaf responds to pressure from groups close to the Islamic Republic.

The official Saudi Press Agency reported that Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan met with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Washington. The two sides discussed regional security and political developments, the situation in Yemen, and the security of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb. The ministers stressed the importance of protecting maritime security and continuing coordination between Riyadh and Washington.

Two informed sources from the aviation industry have stated that all flights from Iran to Turkey are expected to be canceled starting in three days. This is due to US sanctions and increased restrictions on Iranian airlines in the region. A source close to Iran's aviation industry has also confirmed the possible cancellation.

Abbas Araghchi announced a renewed meeting with a Qatari intermediary and expressed hope that the final response from the US would be delivered to Iran via Qatar by Tuesday. He mentioned that ideas to fulfill Iran's conditions have been discussed and will be presented to the American side. Araghchi stated that whenever the US response is ready, it will be conveyed to Iran through Qatar.

The International Organization for Migration announced that since the escalation of conflicts in western Yemen in June, over 145,000 people have been displaced in eight provinces. This number has increased by 15,870 compared to last week. Insecurity continues to cause displacement of families in these areas.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, announced strong US support for Lebanon in implementing the tripartite agreement framework. He described this framework as the only path to lasting peace with Israel. Rubio also emphasized that the US stands with an independent Lebanon free from Hezbollah and Iranian influence.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, called the foiled plot at the Royal Air Force base in Fairford, UK, a very serious threat and saw the trace of a foreign agent in it. Five people were arrested in connection with the incident and later released on bail. Rubio thanked the UK for its cooperation in the case and said more information would be released in the coming days.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, told Fox News that the Islamic Republic is governed by "hardline Shiite clerics" with an apocalyptic view, and such individuals should not have access to nuclear weapons. He called this situation an "unacceptable danger" and added that as the Trump administration's sanctions campaign intensifies, Iran's economy is rapidly heading towards a "great catastrophe." Rubio accused the Islamic Republic of using money to finance Hezbollah, militias in Iraq, support terrorism, build weapons, and carry out "terror plots" worldwide, instead of spending resources on improving people's lives.

Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, said that if Iran had nuclear weapons, it could control the Strait of Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb. He added that Iran could set transit fees and decide who has access to energy. These statements were made in an interview with Fox News.

The Karun Human Rights Organization announced that Tareq Hasnian, a 42-year-old Arab political prisoner, remains in uncertainty six months after his arrest and is deprived of contact with his family. Reports of physical and psychological torture during his interrogation have been received. The organization called for his access to medical services, an independent lawyer, and his release.

Hossein Shariatmadari, editor-in-chief of Kayhan newspaper, condemned Iraq's ban on Iranian flights. He called this action "Ali al-Zaidi's cooperation with America" and "alignment with the Yazid of our time." Shariatmadari added that this ban was proposed by the US Treasury Department and accepted by the Iraqi Prime Minister.

Alireza Kazemi stated that the teachings of the eight-year war, the 12-day war, and the recent war must be included in textbooks. He said students are currently in a battlefield and this is a good opportunity to recognize the enemy and strengthen national identity. Additionally, three books about the 12-day war have been published and provided to students.

Khorasan newspaper, close to Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, wrote that if negotiations fail due to nuclear differences, the Islamic Republic will have the opportunity to use its second plan to carry out preemptive attacks and impose a high-pressure war on Trump before the midterm elections. The newspaper added that this approach would seize the initiative from the enemy and, by raising energy prices, would have severe effects on the outcome of the US elections.

Fatemeh Barmaki won the bronze medal in the +87 kg Kurash category at the 2026 Nagoya Asian Games. She lost in the semifinals to Shi Lio Li Ling from Taiwan and missed the final. Barmaki had previously defeated Yachung Yan in the quarterfinals.

Mahsa Beheshti won the bronze medal in the 86 kg weightlifting category at the 2026 Nagoya Asian Games. She lifted 113 kg in the snatch and secured the bronze with a 146 kg lift in the clean and jerk. Her competitor from Turkmenistan failed to lift the last weight, allowing Beheshti to win the bronze with one less attempt.
